title: Raise the resistor voltage
hook: Change voltage magnitude and predict current magnitude.
misconception: current magnitude stays fixed when voltage magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply I = abs(V)/R to compare current magnitude when voltage magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ohmic resistor with fixed resistance, I = abs(V)/R. When voltage magnitude doubles, current magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model I = abs(V)/R; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ohmic resistor with fixed resistance, with a nonzero initial result. If voltage magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on current magnitude?
recall.why: Apply I = abs(V)/R under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
